newsitem.title: USA: Northeast says Millstone 3 ready by Sept.
newsitem.headline: Northeast says Millstone 3 ready by Sept.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Thursday that it intends to have its Millstone nuclear power unit 3 ready for restart by September.
It also plans to have Millstone unit 2 ready by November, Northeast officials told federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) officials at a meeting here.
But the ultimate reopening of the plants depends upon approval by the NRC.
"For unit 3, we're looking to have the plant physically ready by September 1997," Northeast spokeswoman Deborah Beauchamp told Reuters.

All three Millstone plants have been closed for safety reasons since March of 1996. Northeast said earlier it planned to have one unit ready for restart in the third quarter of this year, one in the fourth quarter, and one in the first quarter of 1998.
But it had not specified which plants would be ready for restart, nor had it given the exact months.
Northeast did not give an exact date when unit 1 would be ready for restart.

Beauchamp said of unit 1, "They're going to have a process called a challenge board. It's an independent process that's going to review how the licensing basis was developed and documented, to make sure they have total confidence in the process that was used to develop that information."
She said this would include a review of 100 position papers covering the design and licensing basis for four systems.
Northeast also told NRC officials the exact dates when each plant's Independent Corrective Action Verification Program (ICAVP) could begin.
Beauchamp said Millstone unit 3's ICAVP was scheduled to start on May 27. For unit 2, it's June 23, and unit 1, at the end of July.
"By those dates, they will be ready for independent (contractor) reviews to begin," she said.
"By ready for restart, we mean that we are prepared, pending the NRC's review, to take the unit into operation," Beauchamp said.
Beauchamp said the NRC's operational safety team (OST) inspection for the 1,150-megawatt unit 3 was scheduled for the end of August.
For 870 MW unit 2, the OST was scheduled for September. "For (660 MW) unit 1, they're not sure yet, because of that challenge board process," she said.
Northeast has said it is spending about $35 million a month in replacement power costs while the Millstone plants are down.
